thread.title: Amazon: New Trends Are Not Priced In - Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)

author: Bluesea Research
title: Amazon: New Trends Are Not Priced In - Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)
text:
Amazon's ( AMZN ) subscription revenues have kept on growing at a rapid pace for the past few quarters. In the latest quarter, subscription revenues grew by 52% on a YoY basis. The secret behind Amazon's success with this segment could be its ability to get a high retention rate even after increasing the cost of Prime membership. The increase in sales of Echo devices has also helped the company in improving revenues from its Amazon Music Unlimited subscription.
While the subscription revenues have been increasing, the growth in shipping costs is trending downwards. In the past few quarters, shipping costs were growing at over 30%. However, in the recent quarter, growth in shipping costs was only 22%. We could see a further reduction in shipping costs as the number of fulfillment centers increase and the online store sales grow at a lower rate .
The trend of over 50% growth in subscription revenues and falling shipping costs should help the company post better profitability in the next couple of quarters. Amazon is also improving its presence in segments like digital payments which provide better long-term moat. Even with a lower revenue growth rate, Amazon's stock should see bullish sentiment as the profitability of the company improves.
Unassailable moat Prime membership has given Amazon an unbeatable moat. It would be very difficult for any company to build similar subscription numbers in e-commerce segment. According to a CIRP report, there are close to 100 million Prime members in US alone. Just three years back, this number was less than 50 million. The rapid growth in membership shows the increase in value proposition for members.
Source: CIRP , WP
According to the census bureau, there are close to 125 million households in the US. This means that Prime membership is reaching four-fifth of the total households. It should be noted that while the absolute number of members has not increased by more than 10% in the last year, the subscription revenues have increased by over 50%.
Source: Company filings
This shows that Amazon is able to extract greater subscription revenues even when the addressable market is getting saturated in US.
Most of the analysts focus on streaming music war between Spotify ( SPOT ) and Apple Music ( AAPL ). But Amazon has been able to increase its market share in this segment, thanks to the popularity of Echo devices.
Fig: Amazon has cornered 12% of market share. Source: MIDiA Research
If the current growth trajectory of Echo devices continues in the next few quarters, we should see a much bigger share from Amazon in music as well as video streaming.
Another side of this story Free shipping is still the most important reason why Prime membership is taken. In a recent survey , 79% of the customers mentioned free shipping as the most important perk for Prime. Hence, we should also look at the cost of this shipping to gauge the success of Amazon's subscription segment.
Fig: Shipping cost from Q2 2017 to Q3 2018.
In the recent quarter, Amazon has been able to rein in its shipping costs substantially. Compared to the year-ago quarter when shipping costs increased by 39%, the shipping cost in the last quarter grew by only 22%. It would be important to see if the current fall in growth rate of shipping costs can be maintained in the future or is it only for the last quarter.
New Services Amazon is trying to add new services which will increase the value proposition for its Prime membership. Earlier this year, Amazon bought PillPack, an internet pharmacy start-up for $1 billion. PillPack is t argeting to get a license in Washington which would allow Amazon to test the services with its own employee base. Amazon could have big plans for this venture as it allows the company to become a must-have service for several segments of its customer base. Shares of pharmacy owners like CVS health and Walgreens Boot Alliance had fallen as the news of the deal was broken out.
Amazon is also expanding the Prime membership in international regions. In June 2018, Amazon launched Prime membership in Australia. The cost of this membership is lower than US. Prime membership costs AU$59 or $44 for annual subscription. Amazon is also expanding its presence in India where a Prime membership costs INR999 or $15 per year. The company is front-loading the benefits in international regions. This means that customers can view all the international content and are given almost similar service levels compared to the US market. This massively improves the value proposition of the company and also allows it to gain membership at a faster pace.
Although the US market has saturated in terms of Prime membership, we should see continuous growth in international markets as new regions are added.
Profitability growth Amazon should be able to push the pedal in terms of profitability growth. It has developed a big moat and has saturated the market in several regions which should allow the company to lower the discounts and improve the margins.
In the last one year, Amazon's EPS estimates have increased by over 100% as more profitable segments show faster growth. This upward revision can continue in 2019 if the company is able to beat consensus estimates in the next few quarters and improve its overall margins.
The stock is trading at 40 times the EPS estimates of 2 fiscal years ahead. Although this is a bit pricey, it should be noted that the company has a number of levers to increase its profitability while showing decent growth rates. This should help the stock to outperform the market in the next year.
Investor Takeaway Amazon is showing over 50% growth in subscription revenues while slowing the growth in shipping costs. This should improve the margins over the next few quarters. Additional subscriptions like Amazon Music Unlimited also provide the company with a long runway for growth. Besides the domestic market in US, Amazon is rapidly expanding in international regions which provide a large addressable base for its Prime membership.
We should see new services and subscriptions from Amazon in the next few quarters. This will increase the profitability of the company and also increase the forward EPS estimates for the stock. It is highly likely that we see another year of bullish run in 2019 with outperformance from the broader market.
